standard.title: Language and images positioning readers
standard.description: explain how language and/or images in texts position readers to respond and form viewpoints
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can identify how language choices and visual features shape reader responses (AC9E7LE03). They have not yet explained the positioning function systematically — how specific language and image choices lead readers toward particular responses and viewpoints rather than others.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how language and/or images in texts position readers to respond in particular ways and form specific viewpoints.

nodes.label: How texts position readers
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain that specific language and image choices in a text are designed to guide readers toward particular responses and viewpoints — not as neutral description but as positioning.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least two specific language or image choices in a provided text are designed to guide the reader toward a particular response or viewpoint.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how language choices (e.g. word choice, tone, narrative perspective, figurative language) and/or visual features in texts work together to position readers to respond in particular ways and form specific viewpoints.
wider: Analyse how a complex picture book combines words and images to position readers to respond emotionally or morally to a character
Compare how two texts on the same subject use different language and visual choices to position readers toward opposing viewpoints on that subject
Examine how First Nations or multicultural authors use positioning strategies to invite non-Indigenous or monocultural readers to adopt unfamiliar perspectives

response_modes.reason: The concept of 'positioning' requires students to adopt a critical stance toward texts that usually feel transparent — to ask 'why is this word chosen rather than another?' Explicit scaffolding of the from-effect-to-cause reasoning is needed: notice the effect first, then reverse-engineer the choices that created it.

success_criteria: Identifies a specific language or image choice in a text.
Explains how that choice is designed to guide the reader toward a particular response or viewpoint, rather than describing the choice neutrally.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 applies the positioning concept to film and multimodal texts. Students who have not established the critical stance — that specific choices are designed to guide responses — will approach film analysis as plot summary or personal reaction rather than as analysis of design choices. The conceptual shift must be established in print before it can travel to multimodal contexts.

nodes.label: Positioning in film and multimodal texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how film and multimodal texts position viewers to respond to characters and events through the interaction of language, image and other modalities.
nodes.minimum_width: Share an opinion about how a film positions the viewer to respond to at least one character, identifying the specific choices (camera angle, music, dialogue, colour, etc.) that create that positioning.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how film and multimodal texts use a combination of language, image, sound and structural features to position viewers to respond to characters, events and issues in particular ways.
wider: Analyse how a film or TV episode uses a sustained combination of visual and linguistic choices to position the viewer to sympathise with one character and distrust another
Compare how the same narrative event is positioned differently in two film adaptations of the same story — examining what choices create different viewer responses
Investigate how documentary filmmakers use visual and language choices to position viewers toward particular conclusions about a real-world subject

response_modes.reason: The positioning concept needs to travel across modalities — from print to image to film. Students who only practise it in print texts may struggle to apply the same critical lens to visual and multimodal texts. Multiple modality contexts build the generalised critical reading skill.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Film analysis is highly engaging for Year 8 students and offers rich material for positioning analysis — the multimodal complexity of film means that positioning operates across multiple simultaneous channels, providing sophisticated analytical territory for advancing students.
success_criteria: Identifies at least two specific choices in a film or multimodal text (e.g. camera angle, word choice, colour, music) and explains how each positions the viewer.
Explains the cumulative effect of these choices on the viewer's response to a character or event.
